name: The Boxed Eave With Nothing In It

severity_by_style.why: The box is the right shape and the entablature is missing from inside it.
As above, and Federal work is more dependent on fine mouldings than Georgian.
Deliberate flattening: broad unmoulded boards, ornament by profile and mass.
A plain fascia and plain soffit are correct.

symptom: A boxed eave of roughly the right depth - soffit, fascia, closed - but with nothing in it. Where the soffit meets the wall there is no frieze board, only a length of J-channel; where the soffit meets the fascia there is no bed mould, only a corner. Two flat boards meeting at ninety degrees, twice.

cause.explanation: The soffit is vented vinyl or aluminium in 12 and 16 in widths, installed by the siding crew, and the only 'moulding' in that trade's kit is J-channel and F-channel, which produce a 3/4 in reveal where a bed mould would produce a 2 1/2 in one. The frieze is skipped for the same reason: the siding runs up to the soffit and is terminated in channel, which is faster than cutting siding to a frieze board and takes no layout.
cause.cost_saved: $3-6 per lineal foot for a frieze and bed mould in primed finger-jointed pine, against nothing. On 150 lf, $450-900 - which is why this fault is worse value than almost any other in the group.

rule_violated.statement: The frieze is one part - 9 in at a 9 ft bay - and the cornice is twice the frieze.
At a 10 ft storey: frieze 10 in, cornice 15 in.

rule_violated.ref: an entablature is architrave, frieze and cornice
rule_violated.statement: The bed mould's job is to hold a shadow at the top of the frieze. Without it the frieze is indistinguishable from siding, and the eave has one shadow line instead of three.

correct_practice: Even the plainest colonial boxed cornice carries a frieze board 8-10 in deep and a bed mould where the soffit meets it. The three shadow lines in order from below are: the top of the frieze (bed mould), the underside of the corona, and the fascia-to-crown junction. Two of the three cost almost nothing. On a masonry house the equivalent is a corbelled brick cornice of a whole number of courses - five courses of 2 2/3 in gauge gives about 13 in, which is why brick cornices come out close to the classical figure without anyone consulting an order.

fixes.right: A frieze board with a bed mould under a boxed soffit, and a crown over the fascia. Four members instead of two.
fixes.cheap: Add the bed mould only. It is the highest-value single moulding on the building because it sits at the top of a tall flat surface and its shadow is what tells the eye the eave has depth. About $2 per lineal foot.
fixes.dishonest: A vinyl 'crown' J-channel or a foam bed mould with a 1/2 in projection. The projection is what makes the shadow, and half an inch makes half an inch of shadow.

test.note: A bed mould at the top of the frieze and a crown over the fascia. A boxed eave with neither shows two flat boards meeting at ninety degrees, twice.

secondary_tests.note: facade-classical puts the frieze at one part - 9 in at a 9 ft bay, 10 in at a 10 ft storey. Below about 0.05 the frieze is indistinguishable from siding.
Vinyl J-channel gives a 3/4 in reveal where a bed mould gives 2 1/2. Half an inch of projection makes half an inch of shadow.

detection: Look at the corner of the house where the eave returns, because there you see the cornice in section. Count the members: a real cornice shows three or more steps between the wall face and the fascia. A boxed eave with nothing in it shows one long flat soffit meeting a flat wall in a straight line, and a photograph taken in raking light will show a single hard edge rather than a stack of parallel shadows.

exceptions.why: Deliberate flattening. The frieze board runs 10-20 in, the trim is broad and unmoulded, and there may be no bed mould at all - ornament in this style is by profile and mass rather than by relief.
exceptions.bounds: The flatness has to be paid for in depth. A Greek Revival eave is bigger, not thinner: the entablature is one quarter to one fifth of the column height and the frieze board is 10-20 in deep. A 6 in fascia with no mouldings is not Greek Revival simplification, it is nothing.

bounds_test.note: The flatness is paid for in depth: the entablature runs one quarter to one fifth of the column height. A 6 in fascia with no mouldings is not Greek Revival simplification, it is nothing.

exceptions.why: A plain fascia and a plain soffit are correct; the eave earns its shadow from 24-36 in of projection.
exceptions.bounds: Rafter tails, purlins or knee braces should be doing the visual work instead.

bounds_test.note: With rafter tails, purlins or knee braces doing the visual work instead.

exceptions.why: The clean soffit with no mouldings is the fastest separation from Craftsman and is definitional.
exceptions.bounds: Only with the 30-48 in overhang and the continuous fascia band drawn unbroken around the whole building.

bounds_test.note: With the continuous fascia band drawn unbroken around the whole building.

exceptions.why: Trim suppression is the rule; a bed mould would be an intrusion.

bounds_test.note: Total suppression, not selective: 2-3 in casing or none, and no corner boards.

confused_with.difference: There is no boxed eave there at all. Here the box exists and is empty.

sources: Asher Benjamin, The American Builder's Companion (1806), plates on cornices
